title: Dependency Air Traffic Control and Readiness Telemetry
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Cross-team roadmap dependencies are currently tracked in scattered docs; we lack a single source of truth that broadcasts readiness signals and pre-flight blockers to downstream owners. This leads to late surprises during cutover windows and risk to SLA deliverables.

Goal: Implement a 'Dependency Air Traffic Control' (DATC) pattern: a lightweight orchestration layer for roadmap dependencies that emits a small set of standardized readiness telemetry signals (e.g., design-approved, infra-provisioned, security-review-clear, e2e-canary-passed). These signals will be visible in the Console Roadmap view and used to gate release rollouts and automated escalation.

Scope:
- Define canonical readiness signal set and allowed values.
- Add dependency metadata fields to Linear tickets (owner, signal timestamps, blockers).
- Implement a telemetry pipeline that consumes signals (webhook or internal events) and surfaces them in a DATC dashboard.
- Create runbook for automated escalation when critical signals are missing within SLA.
- Build a small prototype in Console (read-only) showing per-initiative signal timeline and risk indicator.

Out of scope for this ticket: full two-way automation for rollouts (follow-on), RBAC for signal mutation (separate security ticket).

Success criteria (MVP):
- Teams agree on 6 canonical readiness signals and published definitions in Confluence.
- Telemetry pipeline ingests signals from at least 2 producer types (ENG CI job, Design sign-off webhook).
- DATC dashboard prototype shows timeline and risk color for 10 active initiatives.
- Runbook for escalation authored and validated with SRE and Product Ops.

Metrics to track: percentage of active dependencies with all critical signals present 21 days before release, number of last-minute rollout blockers detected <7 days before cutover, time to escalate when a signal fails SLA.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Confluence spec linked and approved by Eng/Design/Sec/Infra.
2) Telemetry events schema documented and sample events emitted to QA pipeline.
3) Console prototype displays signals and risk score for selected initiatives.
4) Playbook created and a dry-run executed with one initiative by 2025-03-07.
